hints: Differentiate $y = 54x - (2x - 7)^3$ using the chain rule to get $\frac{dy}{dx} = 54 - 6(2x - 7)^2$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the curve equation with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 54 - 3(2x - 7)^2 \times (2) = 54 - 6(2x - 7)^2$$

Differentiate the first derivative to find the second derivative:
$$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -6 \times 2(2x - 7) \times (2) = -24(2x - 7)$$

hints: Solve for $x = 5$ and $x = 2$, then calculate the corresponding $y$-coordinates.
walkthrough:
Set the first derivative equal to zero to locate the stationary points:
$$54 - 6(2x - 7)^2 = 0 \implies 6(2x - 7)^2 = 54 \implies (2x - 7)^2 = 9$$

Evaluate the second derivative at each turning point:
$$\text{At } x = 5: \quad \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -24(10 - 7) = -24(3) = -72 < 0 \implies (5, 243) \text{ is a Local Maximum}$$
$$\text{At } x = 2: \quad \frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -24(4 - 7) = -24(-3) = 72 > 0 \implies (2, 135) \text{ is a Local Minimum}$$
